scope: EXTERNAL corpora only. Local and donor assets (HML_V3 Lean runtime corpus, hml-reasoning-corpus, the locally built mathlib4) are inventoried by other workstreams and appear here only where an external source's classification depends on them.
method: Live primary-source verification on 2026-09-07. Hugging Face facts were read from the Hub API (repo metadata, README frontmatter, file listings, Dataset Viewer size and schema endpoints), not from memory. GitHub and Zenodo facts were read from the repositories, LICENSE files, release records and generation scripts themselves. Project design-history exposure was established by reading docs/CANONICAL_VNEXT_GAP_REPORT.md, docs/FITNESS_V5_SPEC.md, docs/PHASE5_SCHEDULED_DIRECTIVE.md and docs/PROJECT_STATUS.md in this worktree. NOTHING WAS DOWNLOADED: no dataset, no tarball, no model. No local model or LLM call was made. This artifact is research and registry design only.
verification_notes: Where a primary source could not be reached, or two primary sources disagree, the field says UNVERIFIED and the disagreement is recorded rather than resolved by guessing. See the top-level 'unverified' list.

licence_verified is TRUE only when a licence file, repository licence field, or dataset-card frontmatter was actually read. A licence inferred from a paper, a badge, or a sibling repository is recorded as FALSE.

Canonical upstreams are distinguished from mirrors and derivatives throughout. Several widely-used HF datasets in this space are mirrors that alter or drop fields (the LeanDojo mirror drops annotated_tactic and the premise corpus) or that assert a licence the upstream does not (NaturalProofs is commonly cited as MIT; its DATA is not).

Dataset marketing claims are not reported as fact. Where a card's headline count disagrees with the shipped files, both are recorded (e.g. Lean Workbook's 57,231 + 82,893 problems versus the 25,200-row transition parquet).
size_bytes is the download or distribution size in bytes unless the entry says otherwise; size_estimated flags any figure not read from a file listing or size endpoint.

trust_tier uses the vocabulary requested for this registry; trust_tier_arena maps each entry onto the tiers already enforced in arena/provenance.py so the registry can be consumed by existing code without a translation layer.

trust_tier_definitions.VERIFIED_FORMAL: A proof assistant or formal verifier produced or checked the artifact (Lean kernel, Isabelle, Metamath verifiers).
trust_tier_definitions.DETERMINISTICALLY_CHECKED: Checked by an exact mechanical procedure that is not a proof assistant (symbolic algebra, exact-answer match, generator ground truth).
trust_tier_definitions.HUMAN_ANNOTATED: Correctness rests on human labelling or human authorship, with no mechanical check.
trust_tier_definitions.MODEL_GENERATED: Produced by a language model; candidate semantics only, never canonical truth.

trust_tier_map_to_arena_provenance.HUMAN_ANNOTATED: C_CANDIDATE_SEMANTICS or D_ANNOTATION depending on whether the label grounds an oracle
trust_tier_map_to_arena_provenance.note: arena/provenance.py permits only A and B tiers to ground an oracle (ORACLE_GRADE_TIERS).

arena_role_definitions.Sigma_canonical_semantics: Can supply canonical mathematical meaning, i.e. ground truth about what a state IS. Requires executable verification of states.
arena_role_definitions.D_task_distribution: Supplies tasks/problems that define what the Solver is asked to do.
arena_role_definitions.U_library: Supplies the mathematical library the Solver may draw on (declarations, lemmas, simp sets, premises).
arena_role_definitions.verified_trajectories: Supplies before-state / action / after-state triples with a verification path.
arena_role_definitions.natural_language_alignment: Supplies paired natural-language and formal content for studying the NL-to-formal boundary.
arena_role_definitions.reasoning_operation_discovery: Supplies material from which the vocabulary of mathematical operations (theorem selection, rewrite target, instantiation, subgoal choice) can be mined.

GitHub's detector reports NOASSERTION -- ignore it, the file is CC0 1.0. COMPONENTS DIFFER: peano.mm in the same repo is copyright Robert Solovay under the GNU GPL and must be excluded from a pure-CC0 corpus; the Metamath software (metamath-exe, Java, Python) is GPL v2+; website pages are GFDL 1.2+ or CC BY 2.5+.

An exact proved-theorem-only count is UNVERIFIED -- it needs metamath-exe 'show statistics'. The counts on mmset.html (26,000 / 41,000) are badly stale.
domains: ZFC set theory upward: logic, set theory, number theory, real and complex analysis, algebra, topology, Hilbert space
sources.verifier: Many independent verifiers: metamath-exe (C), mmj2 (Java), smetamath-rs/smm (Rust), checkmm (C++), mmverify.py (Python); the site states over a dozen exist. Every change to set.mm is checked by several of them, and mmj2 additionally checks definition soundness.

Design-clean for Arena: named once in docs/PHASE5_SCHEDULED_DIRECTIVE.md as a cheap second Tier-A cross-check, never ingested.
sources.engineering_notes: One 51 MB flat file, no build system, no toolchain to install, and multiple tiny independent verifiers -- by far the lowest-friction second formal system available. Proofs are stored on disk in compressed RPN; metamath-exe 'show proof' expands them into the Step | Hyp | Ref | Expression table where Expression is the state at that step, Ref is the axiom or theorem applied (the transition), and Hyp names which earlier steps feed it. Cost is writing an RPN decompressor or shelling out to a verifier.
sources.notes: Strategically the most interesting non-Lean source in this registry. Metamath's operation algebra is deliberately minimal -- substitution plus modus ponens -- so it is a genuinely DIFFERENT representation of the same mathematics. If a representation effect measured on Lean states replicates on Metamath states, that is strong evidence the effect is about representation rather than about Lean; if it does not replicate, that is equally informative. CC0 removes every redistribution question.

DEVELOPMENT.definition: May be read, inspected, plotted, tuned against and iterated on freely while building instruments and adapters. Reading a DEVELOPMENT item is what burns it: once looked at, it can never be promoted to OOD or RESERVED_EVAL.

TRAINING_CANDIDATE.definition: Eligible to enter SFT/RL data for a future Solver, subject to licence and to the never_train list. Entering training is irreversible for evaluation purposes: a TRAINING_CANDIDATE that is actually trained on becomes HISTORICALLY_EXPOSED.

SCOUT.definition: A small, cheap slice pulled only to answer a structural question about the source itself (does the schema fit, what operations occur, what is the length distribution). Bounded by an explicit item cap declared before the pull. The SCOUT slice is burned; the remainder of the source keeps its own category.

PROMOTION.definition: The single pool on which a candidate representation is scored to decide whether it beats the incumbent. Disjoint from DEVELOPMENT by construction and by group-aware splitting (theorem-level, not item-level, or near-duplicate leakage is guaranteed). Read only at a preregistered decision point, then retired.

OOD.definition: Distribution-shifted relative to DEVELOPMENT along a named, auditable axis (different Lean project, different formal system, later commit date, different problem provenance). Establishes that a representation effect is not an artifact of the development distribution. Requires the shift axis to be stated, not assumed.

ASSURANCE_ONLY.definition: Used solely to check that the harness is not broken -- smoke tests, adapter round-trips, verifier plumbing, encoding checks. Never contributes a scientific number. Contaminated sources are acceptable here precisely because no claim rests on them.

HISTORICALLY_EXPOSED.definition: Already consumed by this project's own design history -- inspected, used to build or calibrate an instrument, or trained on. Permanently disqualified from OOD, PROMOTION and RESERVED_EVAL. Exposure is TRANSITIVE: any dataset derived from an exposed source inherits the exposure (e.g. every mathlib-derived corpus inherits mathlib's exposure, because mathlib goal states were read during Fitness V5 design).

RESERVED_EVAL.definition: Sealed. Not read, not sampled, not previewed, not summarised, by human or agent, until a preregistered unsealing condition fires (a qualified instrument plus a declared hypothesis). The strongest guarantee the project can offer, and the only one that survives an adversarial reading of the record. Unsealing is a one-way door and must be logged in docs/PROJECT_LEDGER.md.

split_category_assignment_notes: No source carries PROMOTION or OOD as a DEFAULT category, and that is deliberate, not an omission. PROMOTION and OOD are DERIVED pools carved out of a source under a preregistered split, never properties a whole corpus is born with. Assigning a source to OOD wholesale would beg the very question OOD is supposed to answer.

Intended derivation path for OOD: miniCTX-v2, non-mathlib configs only. Its valid split becomes DEVELOPMENT once an adapter exists; its test split stays RESERVED_EVAL and is promoted to OOD only at a preregistered decision point, and only once the Solver's training cutoff has been pinned (firewall FW-5).

Intended derivation path for PROMOTION: a theorem-grouped split of LeanDojo Benchmark 4 novel_premises, disjoint from whatever was read during development. Firewall FW-4 applies -- split at the theorem, never at the item, or the same theorem leaks across pools.
A default category is the STRICTEST posture consistent with what is currently known. Sources move down the ladder (RESERVED_EVAL to OOD to DEVELOPMENT to burned) and never back up.

contamination_firewall_rules.detail: mathlib4 goal states were read during Fitness V5 instrument design (docs/FITNESS_V5_SPEC.md: 461 eligible states, 104 used, across 95 mathlib files, via donor MoheetBrain/HML_V3 @ 95e8a26). Therefore mathlib4 is HISTORICALLY_EXPOSED, and so is every corpus derived from it: LeanDojo Benchmark 4 (traced mathlib), miniCTX / miniCTX-v2 'mathlib' config, FormL4 (informalised mathlib theorems), and any mathlib premise-selection extraction. None of these can serve as clean OOD.

contamination_firewall_rules.rule: Naming a dataset in a design document is weaker exposure than reading it.
contamination_firewall_rules.detail: docs/CANONICAL_VNEXT_GAP_REPORT.md names miniF2F, ProofNet, FormL4, Lean Workbook, MATH, AMPS, NuminaMath, LeanDojo and Goedel/Nemotron datasets, but states 'No corpus was downloaded' and that its claims are recalled rather than verified. These are therefore NOT design-exposed by ingestion. They remain exposed by the separate pretraining axis (FW-3).

contamination_firewall_rules.rule: Separate pretraining contamination from design contamination; they have different remedies.
contamination_firewall_rules.detail: Pretraining contamination (the Solver has memorised the items) is not fixed by holding data out -- it is only bounded by temporal cutoff, by novel provenance, or by perturbation. Design contamination (we tuned against it) is fixed only by never having looked. A source can be clean on one axis and filthy on the other. miniF2F is design-clean and pretraining-filthy; mathlib is both.

contamination_firewall_rules.rule: Split at the theorem/problem group, never at the item.
contamination_firewall_rules.detail: Proof-state corpora emit many rows per theorem. Item-level random splitting leaks the same theorem across DEVELOPMENT and PROMOTION and silently inflates every effect. The group-aware splitter already built in hml-reasoning-corpus (claude/max-ev-representation-experiment-v1) should be reused rather than rewritten.

contamination_firewall_rules.rule: A temporal-cutoff OOD claim is only as good as the Solver's stated cutoff.
contamination_firewall_rules.detail: miniCTX-v2 draws theorems committed after 2024-11-28, which is the field's current best temporal-holdout construction. But the Arena Solver is gemma4:12b and its training cutoff is UNVERIFIED in this repository. Until that cutoff is pinned and recorded, miniCTX-v2's OOD status for THIS Solver is a hypothesis, not a fact.

contamination_firewall_rules.rule: Formal verification of a mistranslated statement is not semantic equivalence.
contamination_firewall_rules.detail: Already encoded in arena/provenance.py. Any NL-to-formal source (FormL4, Lean Workbook, NuminaMath-derived formalisations, autoformalised statements generally) is at best Tier C on the semantic-alignment axis even when the Lean side type-checks. Such sources may supply D and training material; they may never supply Sigma.

recommended_next.what_to_take: Zenodo v10 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.12740403), the full 68 MB tarball including corpus.jsonl and the novel_premises split
recommended_next.why: It is the only external source that directly manufactures the task families the project says it needs. Every traced tactic carries state_before, state_after, tactic and annotated_tactic, and annotated_tactic names WHICH premise was used and where it is defined. That yields theorem-selection, rewrite-target and instantiation items with mechanical ground truth, rather than hand-built synthetic mechanisms. Decisively, its generation notebook is pinned at mathlib4 commit 29dcec074de168ac2bf835a77ef68bbe069194c5 -- the SAME commit already built locally with Lean v4.10.0-rc1 and Lean4Repl.olean -- so imported transitions are replayable against the local kernel and rise from Tier B to a locally re-verified Tier A. The novel_premises split additionally guarantees that val/test proofs use at least one premise never seen in any training proof, which is the cleanest available defence against solving premise selection by recall.
recommended_next.information_value: Highest. It converts the project's central open question -- can a Solver make a real mathematical choice -- from a synthetic-probe design problem into a data-extraction problem, and it does so at a commit the project can independently verify.
caveats: HISTORICALLY_EXPOSED via mathlib (firewall FW-1): usable for DEVELOPMENT and PROMOTION, never for OOD.
Licence is CC-BY-2.0 on the old concept DOI and CC-BY-4.0 on the 2025 re-release; pin which tarball was used.
Do NOT use the HF mirror -- it drops annotated_tactic and the premise corpus.

recommended_next.what_to_take: the six NON-mathlib configs (carleson, ConNF, FLT, foundation, HepLean, Seymour); valid split for development, test split SEALED
recommended_next.why: The project has no credible out-of-distribution set at all, and this is the field's best available construction of one: theorems committed after 2024-11-28, drawn from seven real Lean projects rather than from mathlib or competition maths. Apache-2.0, 7.7 MB, and it ships dependencyMetadata (numInFilePremises, numRepositoryPremises, numPremises) so decision difficulty can be stratified without running Lean at all. Independent corroboration of its standing: the 2025 LeanHammer premise-selection work evaluates on mathlib held-out plus miniCTX-v2-test precisely because it is the recognised OOD set.
recommended_next.information_value: Very high, and asymmetric: it is the only thing that can distinguish a real representation effect from an artifact of the mathlib development distribution. It is also the most fragile asset here -- one careless preview destroys it permanently.
caveats: Drop the 'mathlib' config before any OOD use; it inherits mathlib exposure under FW-1.
Firewall FW-5: the OOD guarantee is temporal, and gemma4:12b's training cutoff is UNVERIFIED in this repo, so the guarantee is a hypothesis until that cutoff is pinned.
Contexts span tens of thousands of tokens and collide with the 30,000-rendered-character length-fairness constraint from Fitness V5; budget for truncation policy work.

recommended_next.what_to_take: the whole 406 KB dataset; valid split (2,300 items) as DEVELOPMENT, test split (1,452) sealed
recommended_next.why: Best information value per unit of engineering effort in the entire registry, by a wide margin. It is a balanced binary decision -- is this Lean 4 statement semantically equivalent to this English statement -- with a clean 0.5 chance baseline, and it fits the EXISTING Arena controller (single greedy JSON A/B answer, no reasoning, no search) with essentially no new machinery. Critically, it attacks the specific defect that weakened Fitness V5: on real mathlib depth probes the dumb rule more_frequent_in_state already scores 0.72 against a 0.75 threshold, because deeper identifiers genuinely recur more. Semantic equivalence has no comparable surface proxy, so a representation effect measured here is much harder to explain away as a token-frequency artifact.
recommended_next.information_value: High per byte and per engineer-hour. 406 KB, MIT, and it can plausibly produce a measurable band on the current Solver in a single afternoon, which is exactly what the zero-band result calls for.
caveats: The problem base is ProofNet, which is contaminated; the equivalence LABELS are not, but do not report it as a clean benchmark.
Do not confuse PAug/ProofNetVerif with marcusm117/ProofNet-Verified -- different datasets, different licences, different content.

recommended_next.what_to_take: the single 51 MB set.mm file at a pinned commit SHA; exclude peano.mm (GPL)
recommended_next.why: The cheapest possible second formal system, and the only route to the strongest claim the project could make. Game R asks whether representation causes capability; a result measured only on Lean states is always open to the objection that it is a fact about Lean. Metamath encodes the same mathematics with a deliberately minimal operation algebra -- substitution plus modus ponens -- and its proofs expand to explicit Step / Hyp / Ref / Expression tables, i.e. native state transitions with the applied theorem named. One flat CC0 file, no toolchain to install, and a dozen independent verifiers to check against.
recommended_next.information_value: High but deferred: this is the replication instrument, valuable only once a Lean-side effect exists to replicate. Its cost is low enough that it should be scoped now rather than after.
caveats: Proofs are stored in compressed RPN; expanding them means writing a decompressor or shelling out to metamath-exe.
Rolling database with no releases -- a commit SHA must be pinned or the corpus is unreproducible.
peano.mm in the same repo is GPL and breaks a pure-CC0 corpus.

recommended_next.what_to_take: wkbk_1009.parquet ONLY (4.6 MB, 25,200 rows); do not pull lean_workbook.json (94.5 MB)
recommended_next.why: The best available NON-mathlib source of before/after Lean proof states, at 4.6 MB and Apache-2.0. Its role is a control, not a headline: if a representation effect appears on mathlib transitions but vanishes on contest-problem transitions, the effect is a fact about mathlib's writing conventions rather than about representation. That is a cheap and genuinely falsifying check.
recommended_next.information_value: Moderate but well targeted -- it buys a distributional control that no amount of extra mathlib data can buy.
caveats: Built at Lean v4.8.0-rc1, not the local v4.10.0-rc1; replay will need a version bridge.
Autoformalised, so firewall FW-6 applies: the Lean side type-checks but NL-to-formal equivalence is Tier C.
The HF card's 57,231 + 82,893 problem figures describe the JSON statement pool, not the 25,200-row transition parquet.

low_value_for_us.why: 16.4 GB compressed and 56.7 GB uncompressed of unverified web text with no structure, no states, no transitions and no verifier. It IS a pretraining corpus, so contamination is total by construction, and the project is not pretraining a model. Its per-document licences are explicitly not cleared (ODC-By 1.0 plus Common Crawl ToU, underlying licences unaltered), which is a live redistribution hazard for no scientific return.

low_value_for_us.verdict: AVOID as measurement; marginal as future SFT
low_value_for_us.why: 1.7 GB and roughly 900,000 informal problems with no proof states, no transitions and no verifier beyond final-answer matching. It is one of the most heavily used math post-training corpora in existence, so a 12B-class Solver has plausibly been trained on it or its descendants. Popularity here is precisely the disqualifier.

low_value_for_us.verdict: AVOID except as the contaminated arm of a GSM8K/GSM1K contamination probe
low_value_for_us.why: Saturated, universally memorised, and its reasoning content is arithmetic sequencing rather than mathematical choice. There is no theorem to select, no rewrite target, no instantiation and no subgoal -- so it cannot exercise the very capability the next experiments are designed to measure. Its representation space is effectively one-dimensional.

Maximal contamination, plus an accepted DMCA takedown from Art of Problem Solving (2025-01-02) asserting that over 10,000 of the 12,500 problems match its proprietary Alcumus content and that AoPS staff wrote ALL the solutions, with removal of derivatives requested. The canonical HF copy is disabled. Nominal MIT does not settle a contested right to grant. A research project gains nothing here worth that exposure.

23 GB uncompressed of largely templated Mathematica-generated items behind a Google Drive link, with only 37 of 100 generator scripts producing step-by-step solutions and no AMPS-specific licence. Its single interesting property -- generator-backing, which could yield fresh uncontaminated items -- is UNVERIFIED, because the paper never states the generators ship. 23 GB of templates is a poor trade against 4.6 MB of real Lean tactic transitions.

Widely cited and commonly mislabelled MIT: MIT covers only the code, while the data is CC BY-SA 4.0 (ProofWiki) plus GFDL v1.2 (Stacks) plus CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (Trench, NON-COMMERCIAL). Three copyleft sources and one non-commercial source in one release. And it has no verifier at all -- it is entirely natural language -- so it can never ground Sigma or supply measurement truth.

Doubly disqualified. Contamination: the most-reported formal proving benchmark of the last five years, mirrored into countless training corpora. Quality: arXiv:2511.03108 (2025-11) finds formal/informal discrepancies in MORE THAN HALF the problems, with end-to-end accuracy of 36% on the original versus 70% on a corrected version. So it cannot support a capability claim or a natural-language alignment claim. Keep 488 well-formed statements as harness smoke tests and nothing else.

Strictly dominated by Metamath set.mm as a second formal system: AFP distributes no intermediate proof states, so extracting them means installing and running a whole second proof assistant, against per-entry BSD/LGPL licences that must be filtered one by one. Metamath gives the same cross-system replication for one CC0 flat file.

mathlib informalised by Gemini-1.5-Pro: it inherits mathlib's design exposure under FW-1 so it can never be OOD, and its English side is model-generated so under FW-6 its semantics are capped at Tier C. On top of that the repo has no LICENSE file and the CC BY 4.0 claim is README prose only.

Both ship WHOLE PROOFS, not per-step states, which is exactly the wrong granularity for a project whose unit of analysis is the transition. Extracting states would mean replaying every proof through Lean -- which the local mathlib build already does more cheaply and at a commit the project controls. Both also have unresolved dataset licences.

Scientifically the most interesting informal source here (800,000 human step-level -1/0/+1 labels), but its training data contains 4,500 of the 5,000 MATH test problems, so it has already leaked the standard test set into the public pool; and its problem base carries the AoPS claim. Nothing built on it can be held out cleanly.
